items.title: Police didn’t have chance to save man who fell to his death in Mississauga: SIU
items.summary: The province’s Special Investigations Unit has ended its probe into an incident in which a man fell to his death from the balcony of a Mississauga condo this past summer. ” The SIU is called in whenever there’s a serious injury or death during interactions between members of the public and police officers. The provincial watchdog agency said Peel police officers were dispatched to the central Mississauga condo building following a July 29 call from a woman who reported her boyfriend had assaulted her. An INSAUGA Canada story at the time of the incident noted the building is located on Kingsbridge Garden Circle, just north of Highway 403. In its narrative of events, the SIU said responding police officers received no answer after knocking on the door to the condo unit and identifying themselves. ” Continuing, the SIU said the officers “called out the man’s name and announced their presence. ” The man, 34, had placed a chair near the balcony railing “and was seen climbing onto it. As the officer crossed the room towards the sliding glass door, he called out to the man to stop him,” the agency said in recounting the events.

items.title: Popular trails will be upgraded in Mississauga to extend life by 25 years
items.summary: Mississauga is upgrading two popular trails as part of a plan to extend their service life by up to 25 years. The City of Mississauga said in a project update it’s “undertaking trail reconstruction improvements” at two locations in the city’s north end: “These improvements will create safer, more accessible connections throughout the neighbourhood, supporting walking, cycling, recreation and everyday travel,” the city said in its online update. ” Ward 9 Coun. Martin Reid said residents should be aware that ongoing construction may lead to temporary trail closures while the work is being completed. ” The municipality said the reconstructed trails will be built to current city standards, “providing reliable, low-maintenance infrastructure for the community. “The upgrades are expected to extend the service life of the trails by approximately 20 to 25 years, while helping to reduce future maintenance requirements,” the city added. Officials said they’ll use advance notice signs to let residents know of any upcoming temporary trail closures or construction activity that may impact them.

items.title: Two events set to take over one of Mississauga’s busiest neighbourhoods
items.summary: Two very different events, one celebrating a significant annual holiday and the other inviting guests to relive the past, will take place just steps apart in Mississauga this weekend. Diwali RazzMatazz and Nostalgia Fest Expo are both taking place from Oct. 9 to 11, with the events happening in Mississauga’s downtown core–a place that’s best known for being home to the city’s main entertainment space and one of the province’s busiest shopping centres. At Mississauga Celebration Square, Diwali RazzMatazz will offer three days of Indian culture, music, food and family entertainment. Hosted annually by the Indo-Canada Arts Council (ICAC) since 2014, the festival attracts more than 50,000 attendees each year, according to organizers. Visitors can expect Bollywood performances, live musical concerts, cultural dance showcases and a Diwali Bazaar, along with kids’ activities and rides. Meanwhile, Nostalgia Fest Expo will take over the Square One Event Hall for three days of trading cards, collectibles, entertainment and nostalgia. Magic: The Gathering and sports cards, among other trading card games. The event will also feature toys, figures, anime merchandise and other nostalgic collectibles, along with special guests and celebrity appearances.

items.title: Mississauga lottery player takes lump sum after scoring lifetime prize: 'out-of-this-world experience'
items.summary: The winning ticket was purchased at Apple Party Mart on North Service Road. Dennis Cidade of Mississauga wins a Daily Grand second prize of $25,000 a year for life in the Sept. 3 draw. He opted for the lump sum of $500,000. A Mississauga man who has been playing the lottery for about 30 years has won his first major prize playing Daily Grand. Dennis Cidade, 50, won the Daily Grand second prize of $25,000 a year for life in the Sept. 3 draw. Instead of the annuity prize, he opted for a lump-sum payment of $500,000. He found he won the lottery after breakfast one day. “At first, I couldn’t process it,” he said in an Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corp. news release. ” His mom was the first person he shared the news with.

items.title: Brampton default mortgage home listings double Mississauga’s total so far this year
items.summary: The number of default mortgage properties listed for sale in Brampton so far this year doubles the total in neighbouring Mississauga, with one real estate market analyst saying more “mortgage distress” is yet to come. A “power of sale” can happen when a homeowner defaults on their mortgage, leading to the lender selling the property in order to recover any outstanding debts. 7 million in Brampton a few years ago that traded hands last month at a nearly $750 loss. The home on Gulfbrook Circle in Brampton was bought in February 2022 for $1,715,000, and listed multiple times in 2025 with an asking price of $1,429,000, and later lowered to $1,199,900. The detached property was listed again in August for $969,900 and sold last month for 968,000. Brampton had 45 active power of sale listings on Oct. com. And while Toronto has the most active power of sale listings currently on the market with 179, Brampton has had the most new power of sale listings so far this year with a total that doubles the amount of new default mortgage listings in Mississauga. Canadian real estate watcher John Flynn posted data from the Matrix multiple listing service on X, saying there have been 406 new Brampton power of sale listings in 2026 compared to 203 in Mississauga.

items.title: Mississauga and Brampton Hospitals Among 26 Sites Getting $47M Push to Cut ER Wait Times
items.summary: According to Insauga, the Ontario government announced Wednesday it will spend more than $47 million over four years on a new Emergency Department Action Team, or EDAT, that will work directly with 26 hospitals across the province to cut emergency room wait times. Insauga reports Mississauga and Brampton hospitals are among the sites included, specifically William Osler Health System's Brampton Civic Hospital and Etobicoke General Hospital, along with Trillium Health Partners' Credit Valley Hospital and Mississauga Hospital. The province said the initiative responds to emergency departments facing sustained pressure from rising patient volumes, more complex cases and growing demands on the health-care system. EDAT will examine how patients move through emergency departments, from initial assessment and diagnostic testing through to admission or discharge, looking for what's causing delays along the way. The province said the 26 hospitals were chosen based on factors including emergency department volumes and the potential for improvements to benefit the largest number of patients. Insauga reports operational and performance indicators, along with representation across different hospital types and regions, also factored into the selection.

items.title: Mississauga's City Centre Lands Among GTA's Cheapest Neighbourhoods to Buy a Home
items.summary: According to Insauga, real estate platform Wahi's monthly ranking of the Greater Toronto Area's least expensive neighbourhoods placed Mississauga's City Centre among the cheapest places to buy last month, the only Peel Region community on the list. Wahi found City Centre's median sold price was $428,750 in September, with 30 homes selling over an average of about 34 days on the market. Insauga reports North York's Flemington Park topped the overall list with a median price of $383,000, where six homes sold in an average of 26 days, while Etobicoke's Woodbine ranked second at $402,000 with five sales averaging 42 days. Wahi builds its rankings each month using median home sale prices in GTA neighbourhoods with five or more sales. Insauga notes the most expensive neighbourhoods on Wahi's list tended to be older Toronto communities and areas known for large properties, a contrast to the bargains showing up amid the broader market's ongoing slowdown this fall.

items.title: Mississauga musicians: add your track to the City’s Music 311 playlist
items.summary: Mississauga musicians are invited to apply for a chance to share their music with thousands of listeners across City channels and receive $300 if selected. Through the City’s Music 311 program, 12 songs will be selected to showcase the diverse styles, genres and voices of Mississauga’s music community. Selected artists will receive a $300 payment and promotion on the City’s website and social media channels. The program turns everyday City touchpoints into opportunities to discover local music. With 311 receiving up to 950 calls a day and 250,000 calls each year, selected songs may be heard by thousands of callers while they wait for a customer service representative.
